# Setting Up Statement and Invoice Email Content

You can control the sender, subject and message used when OrderHub emails statements and invoices. Labs with multiple brands can use one default setup for every brand, then replace individual fields for selected brands.

---

## Open the Email Content Settings

1. Go to **Settings → Accounts**.
2. Scroll to **Email content**.
3. Use **Brand / Website** to choose which settings you want to edit.
4. Choose either **Statement email** or **Invoice email**.

![Email Content for Accounts](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/36b633a0-a2e9-4656-a857-75619eae9962.png)

---

## Which Settings Get Used

Every statement and invoice email uses the settings belonging to the customer's brand:

- **Invoices** follow the brand on the order.
- **Statements** follow the brand set on the customer's company — or, when the company has no brand set, the one brand shared by their orders.

If the brand can't be determined, the **Default (All Brands)** settings are used. Blank fields fall back to the default.

* Note: a customer's brand comes from their company, not from the customer record. To set it, open the company → **Edit** → **Brand**.
* Note: if a customer's orders are spread across more than one brand and no brand is set on the company, the brand can't be worked out — set it on the company so statements use the brand you expect.

---

## Set Up the Default for All Brands

Select **Default (All Brands)** under **Brand / Website**.

These settings are used by every brand unless you create an override for a particular brand.

Complete the fields you need:

| Field | What it controls |
|---|---|
| **From email** | The address customers see as the sender. Leave it blank to use the organization email. |
| **From name** | The sender name customers see in their inbox. |
| **BCC (optional)** | An address that receives a hidden copy of each email. |
| **Subject** | The email subject line. |
| **Message body (HTML)** | The message displayed in the email. Leave it blank to use the built-in message. |

Set up **Statement email** and **Invoice email** separately. Changing one does not change the other.

When finished, select **Save Accounts settings**.

---

## Use Different Email Content for a Brand

If your lab operates more than one brand:

1. Open **Brand / Website**.
2. Select the brand you want to customise.
3. Choose **Statement email** or **Invoice email**.
4. Enter only the fields that should be different from **Default (All Brands)**.
5. Leave all other fields blank so they continue using the default.
6. Select **Save Accounts settings**.

For example, a brand could have its own **From name** and **Subject**, while continuing to use the default **From email**, **BCC** and **Message body (HTML)**.



OrderHub shows which fields are overridden for the selected brand. If no fields have been completed, it shows:

> This brand uses the default settings for everything.

---

## How Blank Fields Work

Blank fields behave differently depending on what is selected:

| Selection | What a blank field does |
|---|---|
| **Default (All Brands)** | Uses the organization email or the built-in email content, where available. |
| A specific brand | Inherits that field from **Default (All Brands)**. |

This means you do not need to copy the complete default message into every brand.

---

## Return a Brand to the Default

To remove a brand's custom settings:

1. Select the brand under **Brand / Website**.
2. Choose **Statement email** or **Invoice email**.
3. Select **Clear override (then save)**.
4. Select **Save Accounts settings**.

The brand will then use **Default (All Brands)** for every field in that email type.

---

## Using Placeholders

Placeholders insert information from the statement, invoice, customer or organization when the email is sent.

### Statement email placeholders

- `{{company_name}}`
- `{{org_name}}`
- `{{statement_date}}`
- `{{total_due}}`
- `{{download_url}}`
- `{{link_expires}}`

Example subject:

`Statement of account — {{statement_date}}`

### Invoice email placeholders

- `{{company_name}}`
- `{{customer_name}}`
- `{{org_name}}`
- `{{invoice_number}}`
- `{{invoice_date}}`
- `{{due_date}}`
- `{{order_number}}`
- `{{total_amount}}`
- `{{download_url}}`

Example subject:

`Invoice {{invoice_number}} from {{org_name}}`

Enter placeholders exactly as shown, including both pairs of curly brackets.

---

## Check Which Settings Will Be Used

Before sending to a customer, use **Accounts → Test send**.

1. Choose **Invoice** or **Statement**.
2. Find the document you want to test.
3. Select **Check details**.
4. Review the **From**, **To**, **CC**, **BCC**, subject and PDF link.
5. Check whether the email is using **Default (All Brands)** or the selected brand's own settings.
6. Select **Send test** when the details are correct.

A test does not mark the invoice or statement as sent.

---

## Good to Know

- **Statement email** and **Invoice email** have separate settings.
- Start by completing **Default (All Brands)**.
- For a specific brand, enter only the fields that need to be different.
- Blank brand fields inherit from the default.
- Remember to select **Save Accounts settings** after making changes.
- The customer or company must be associated with the correct brand for its brand-specific settings to be used.
